# Problem 1

# Problem 2

Answers will vary. The pdf, $f(y|w)$ is the distribution of observations given a fixed $w$. The likelihood, $L(w|y)$, treats the data as observed and lets $w$ vary.

# Problem 3

Answers will vary. Starting with a distribution and unknown parameters, calculate the joint distribution. Then, treat this as the likelihood (observe data and let $w$ vary). Take the natural log of the likelihood. Take derivatives and set to zero for each unknown parameter and solve jointly. 

# Problem 4

$E[X^2]$ computation

$$
E[X^2]=\int_0^\infty x^2\,\frac{1}{\beta}e^{-x/\beta}\,dx=\frac{1}{\beta}\int_0^\infty x^2\,e^{-x/\beta}dx
$$

Use integration by parts with $u=x^2$ and $dv=e^{-x/\beta}dx$, so $du=2x\,dx$ and $v=-\beta e^{-x/\beta}$:

$$
=\frac{1}{\beta}\Big[\Big[-x^2e^{-x/\beta}\Big]_0^\infty-\int_0^\infty -2x\beta e^{-x/\beta}\,dx\Big]
$$

The term $\Big[-x^2e^{-x/\beta}\Big]_0^\infty$ becomes zero. Move $2\beta$ outside the integral and $\frac{1}{\beta}$ inside the integral

$$
=2\beta\int_0^\infty x\,\frac{1}{\beta}e^{-x/\beta}\,dx=2\beta\,E[X]=2\beta\cdot\beta=2\beta^2 
$$

Variance computation:

$$
V(X)=E[X^2]-\big(E[X]\big)^2=2\beta^2-\beta^2=\beta^2
$$

# Problem 5

Answers will vary. Since each $X_i$ is independent, the joint distribution is the product of the distribution functions. $P(A\cup B)=P(A)P(B)$ by the independence assumption.

# Problem 6

$$
L(\beta \mid \mathbf{x})=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\frac{1}{\beta}e^{-x_i/\beta}
=\beta^{-n}\exp\!\left(-\frac{1}{\beta}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i\right).
$$

$$
\ell(\beta)=\ln L(\beta \mid \mathbf{x})
=-n\ln\beta-\frac{1}{\beta}\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i .
$$

# Problem 9

If the readings are truly independent, then the measurement of one does not depend on the other one. We also know that $Cov(X,Y)=0$ if $X$ and $Y$ are independent.

To solve this problem, we need the joint distribution, marginal distributions, expectations of marginal distributions and $X_1X_2$

Since $X_1$ and $X_2$ both come from the same exponential distribution, we already have their expectations and variances calculated.

*Marginal means:*
$$
E[X_1]=\beta,\qquad
E[X_2]=\beta
$$

*Marginal variances:*
$$
V(X_1)=\beta^2,\qquad
V(X_2)=\beta^2
$$

To get the joint distribution, take the product of the two exponential distributions.

*Joint distribution:*

$$
f(x_1,x_2)=f_{X_1}(x_1)\,f_{X_2}(x_2)=\frac{1}{\beta^2}e^{-(x_1+x_2)/\beta},\quad x_1,x_2>0 
$$

$E[X_1X_2]$ can be found by integrating over the product of $x_1x_2$ and the joint distribution.

*Expected product:*
$$
E[X_1X_2]=\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_0^\infty x_1x_2\,f_{X_1}(x_1)f_{X_2}(x_2)\,dx_1\,dx_2 .
$$

Lastly,

$$
\text{Cov}(X_1,X_2)=E[X_1X_2]-E[X_1]\,E[X_2],
\qquad
\text{Corr}(X_1,X_2)=\frac{\text{Cov}(X_1,X_2)}{\sqrt{V(X_1)\,V(X_2)}} .
$$

# Problem 10

$$
P(X\le x)=\int_0^x\frac{1}{\beta}e^{-t/\beta}\,dt
=\Big[-e^{-t/\beta}\Big]_0^x=1-e^{-x/\beta},
$$

$$
F(x)=
\begin{cases}
0, & x < 0,\\
1-e^{-x/\beta} & x\gt 0
\end{cases}
$$

With $\hat{\beta}=1.564$, 

$$
P(X>1)=1-P(X\leq 1)=1-(1-e^{-1/1.564})=0.5276162
$$
